rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is told to eat dates, drink from the stream, and find comfort in Jesus.
rows.anchor: أي فكلي من الرطب، واشربي من السري، (وقري عينا) بعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For delight, قررت به عينا has a fatḥa in the imperfect; for settling in a place, قررت has a kasra.
rows.anchor: يقال: قررت به عينا أقر بفتح القاف في المستقبل. وقررت في المكان أقر - بكسر القاف - في المستقبل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عينا is accusative as a specification (tamyīz).
rows.anchor: و (عينا) منصوب على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The received ترين is without hamza; ترأين with hamza is linguistically good but unattested and unsuitable for Qur’anic recitation, which follows transmission.
rows.anchor: بألف ولم يقرأ بالألف أحد وهي جيدة بالغة لكنها لا يجوز في القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, وأرأي with hamza is possible linguistically but is not recited; the transmitted reading is أرى.
rows.anchor: ويجوز وأرأي بالألف، ولا تقرأ بها، لفظها أرأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ترين, tā marks the feminine, the underlying form is ترآين, and the yā is moved to avoid two adjacent sukūns; the nūn is emphatic.
rows.anchor: والتاء علامة التأنيث، والأصل ترآين، والياء حركت لالتقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same form is used in the feminine imperative اخشين زيدا.
rows.anchor: وكذلك تقول للمرأة اخشين زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here صوما means silence.
rows.anchor: معنى (صوما) صمتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نذرت is used for vowing; نذرت بالقوم can also mean learning of people and preparing for them.
rows.anchor: نذرت النذر أنذره وأنذره، ونذرت بالقوم أنذر إذا علمت بهم فاستعددت لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فريا means something immense; يفري الفري describes someone doing work with exceptional intensity or accomplishment.
rows.anchor: أي شيئا عظيما، يقال فلان يفري الفري إذا كان يعمل عملا يبالغ فيه

rows.speaker: أهل الكتاب
rows.claim: The People of the Book objected that Mary could not be Aaron's sister because she and Aaron were separated by six hundred years.
rows.anchor: أن أهل الكتاب قالوا: كيف تقولون أنتم: مريم أخت هارون وبينهما ستمائة سنة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet explained that people were named after prophets and righteous people, so Mary's brother was named Aaron.
rows.anchor: فقيل ذلك لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال: إنهم كانوا يسمون بأسماء الأنبياء والصالحين

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another explanation takes “sister of Aaron” as likeness in piety; Aaron was a righteous man among her people, and his funeral reportedly drew forty thousand men each named Aaron.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنهم عنوا بأخت هارون في الصلاح والدين، ويروى أن هارون هذا الدين كان رجلا من قومها صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj regards the explanation attributed to the Prophet as decisive.
rows.anchor: والذي في هذا عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's gesture redirected the people to speak with Jesus; their question about addressing an infant in the cradle confirms this.
rows.anchor: بأن جعلوا الكلام معه، ودل على أنها أشارت إليه في الكلام قولهم (كيف نكلم من كان في المهد صبيا)

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats كان as redundant: how can they speak to an infant in the cradle who cannot understand or speak, though every person was once an infant?
rows.anchor: اللغو، المعنى كيف نكلم من في المهد صبيا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take كان to mean occurred or came into being: how can they speak to a child newly created in the cradle?
rows.anchor: في معنى وقع وحدث. المعنى على قول هؤلاء: كيف نكلم صبيا قد خلق في المهد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best analysis makes من conditional and جزاء, with صبيا a circumstantial accusative: if one is an infant in the cradle, how can one speak to him?
rows.anchor: المعنى: من يكن في المهد صبيا - ويكون (صبيا) حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy for that conditional reading is asking how one can address someone who neither hears nor understands.
rows.anchor: كما تقول من كان لا يسمع ولا يعقل فكيف أخاطبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jesus leaned on his left side, pointed with his index finger, and then spoke.
rows.anchor: وروى أن عيسى عليه السلام لما أومأت إليه اتكأ على يساره وأشار بسبابته فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مباركا means a teacher of good.
rows.anchor: وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت) أي معلمأ للخير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زكاة here means purification.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الزكاة ههنا الطهارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دمت and دمت are both accepted forms.
rows.anchor: - دمت، ودمت جميعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: برا is coordinated with مباركا: God made Jesus blessed and dutiful to his mother.
rows.anchor: (وبرا) عطف على (مباركا)، المعنى وجعلني مباركا وبرا بوالدتي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سلام may mean the verbal noun of سلمت and general safety, the plural of سلامة, or one of God's names.
rows.anchor: فالسلام مصدر سلمت سلاما، ومعناه عموم العافية والسلامة، والسلام جمع سلامة، والسلام اسم من أسماء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite سلام can begin a sentence because it is frequently used and generic nouns can convey nearly the benefit of definiteness.
rows.anchor: وسلام مما ابتدئ به في النكرة، لأنه اسم يكثر استعماله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because سلام appeared earlier without the article, repeating it as السلام is better, though either form is possible.
rows.anchor: بغير ألف ولام كان الأحسن أن يرد ثانية بالألف واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The referent is Jesus son of Mary, not the Christians' claim that he is God's son or himself divine.
rows.anchor: عيسى ابن مريم لا ما يقول النصارى من أنه ابن الله وأنه إله - جل الله وعز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative قول الحق means “he is the statement of truth”; with accusative it means “I state the truth.”
rows.anchor: بالرفع، ويجوز (قول الحق) بالنصب، فمن رفع فالمعنى هو قول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من ولد is an accusative object construction and من reinforces the negation; it excludes both one child and multiple children.
rows.anchor: (من ولد) في موضع نصب، والمعنى أن يتخذ ولدا، و (من) مؤكدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سبحانه means declaring God free of evil.
rows.anchor: (سبحانه). معناه تنزيها له من السوء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day of the great gathering is the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يعنى به يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will hear and see clearly on Resurrection because they will witness resurrection and God's command directly; in worldly life obedience requires thought, which they neglected for amusement and desire.
rows.anchor: لأنهم شاهدوا من البعث وأمر الله عز وجل ما يسمع ويبصر بغير إعمال فكر وتروية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم الحسرة is the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: (يوم الحسرة) يوم القيامة،

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A report depicts death as a speckled ram brought before the people of Hell and Paradise, recognized and slaughtered; both groups are then told they will live forever without death.
rows.anchor: أتى بالموت في صورة كبش أملح فيعرض على أهل النار فيشرئبون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وهم في غفلة means they are heedless in worldly life.
rows.anchor: (وهم في غفلة). أي هم في الدنيا في غفلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to recall Abraham's story and account in the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أي اذكر في الكتاب الذي أنزل عليك وهو القرآن قصة إبراهيم وخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صديق is an intensive form for truthfulness; it also names anyone who affirms God's oneness and messengers and acts accordingly, as in Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq's title.
rows.anchor: الصديق اسم للمبالغة في الصدق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In address the Arabs say يا أبة and يا أمة, but do not use أبتي or أمتي in ordinary reported speech; the pause form is يا أبه.
rows.anchor: الوقف عليه يا أبه بالهاء، والعرب تقول في النداء يا أبة، ويا أمة ولا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh compare يا أبة to vocatives such as يا عمة and يا خالة; the form can address a male or female.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل وسيبويه أنه بمنزلة قولهم يا عمة ويا خالة، وأن أبة للمذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual أبوان shows that the mother shares in the term of parenthood; the cited Qur'anic wording is “his parents inherited him.”
rows.anchor: والدليل على أن للأم حظا في الأبوة أنه يقال أبوان، قال الله عز وجل: (وورثه أبواه).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form also parallels feminine-looking descriptors used for males, such as رجل ربعة and غلام يفعة.
rows.anchor: وزعم أنه بمنزلة قولهم رجل ربعة، وغلام يفعة.

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: The hāʾ in أبة replaces the possessive yāʾ of يا أبي or يا أمي; it occurs only in address because yāʾ is often dropped there.
rows.anchor: وأن الهاء في أبة، عوض من ياء الإضافة من يا أبي ومن يا أمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possessive yāʾ may be omitted in vocative يا أب, but not in non-vocative قال أب when “my father” is intended.
rows.anchor: تقول: يا أب لا تفعل، ولا تقل قال أب كذا وكذا تريد قال أبي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feminine forms can describe males, as in امرأة طالق وطاهر; نفس is feminine even when three persons are called ثلاثة أنفس.
rows.anchor: والمؤنث قد يوصف بالمذكر كقولهم امرأة طالق وطاهر، ويقال ثلاثة أنفس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, يا أبتا is intended: its alif replaces the possessive yāʾ and is deleted because that yāʾ would itself be deleted.
rows.anchor: فمن فتح حذف الألف التي أبدلت من ياء الإضافة أراد يا أبتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects that neither hear, see, nor benefit are idols.
rows.anchor: يعني الصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim's saying that knowledge came to him indicates that revelation had come to him.
rows.anchor: يدل أنه كان قد أتاه الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صراطا سويا means a straight path.
rows.anchor: ومعنى: (صراطا سويا). أي طريقا مستقيما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping Satan means obeying him in the disbelief and sins he entices people toward.
rows.anchor: معنى عبادة الشيطان - والله أعلم - طاعته فيما يسول من الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لأرجمنك can mean “I will insult you”; يرمي or يرجم someone can mean insulting him, as in the accusation expressed by يرمون المحصنات.
rows.anchor: يقال: فلان يرمي فلانا ويرجم فلانا معناه يشتمه.

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Although لأرجمنك could mean stoning Abraham to death, the reported interpretation is that his father threatens to insult him.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون (لأرجمنك) لأقتلنك رجما، والذي عليه التفسير أن الرجم ههنا الشتم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حفيّا means kind and gentle; تحفى به describes treating someone with care and kindness.
rows.anchor: معناه لطيفا، يقال: قد تحفى فلان بفلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving Abraham and Isaac a noble tongue means preserving good praise for them, as in Abraham's prayer for later generations.
rows.anchor: أي أبقينا لهم ثناء حسنا، وكذلك قوله: (واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both مخلصا and مخلصا are read: with fatḥa, God selected Moses and purified him; with kasra, Moses made himself sincere in God's unity and obedience.
rows.anchor: والمخلص - بفتح اللام الذي أخلصه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نجيا means one speaking privately; the report says Moses was brought close enough to hear the pen writing the Torah.
rows.anchor: معناه مناجيا. وجاء في التفسير أن الله عز وجل قربه حتى سمع صريف القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses was brought close in rank to hear God's speech, as expressed by the Qur'anic statement that God spoke to Moses directly.
rows.anchor: ويجوز - والله أعلم - أن يكون، مثل: (وكلم الله موسى تكليما) أي قربه في المنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هارون is indeclinable when definite because it is a foreign proper name.
rows.anchor: هارون لا ينصرف في المعرفة لأنه اسم أعجمي وهو معرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismāʿīl's أهل means his whole community, whether related to him or not; this is true of every prophet's people.
rows.anchor: أهله جميع أمته، من كانت بينه وبينه قرابة أو من لم تكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مرضوا is linguistically possible but excluded from Qur'anic recitation because it conflicts with the consonantal codex.
rows.anchor: أصله مرضوا، وهو جائز في اللغة غير جائز في القرآن لأنه مخالف للمصحف

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, and the Basrans explain مرضي through a pattern that changes final wāw to yāʾ after a preceding still wāw; they also attest مرضو and forms like أرض مسنوة/مسنية.
rows.anchor: والخليل وسيبويه وجميع البصريين يقولون

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One alternative derives مرضي from رضيت, saying the verb's shift from wāw to yāʾ carries into the derived form.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: لما كان الفعل منه رضيت فانتقل من الواو إلى الياء. صار مرضيا.

rows.speaker: بعض العرب
rows.claim: Some Arabs use both رضيان and رضوان in the dual; the first supports only مرضي, while the second permits both مرضو and مرضي.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن بعض العرب يقول في تثنية رضى رضيان ورضوان

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: One report says Idrīs was raised to the fourth heaven.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أيضا أنه رفع إلى السماء الرابعة

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A report says Idrīs asked the Angel of Death to seek God's raising him, then argued from the promised passage through Hell and the assurance that the people of Paradise will not be expelled; God kept him in Paradise.
rows.anchor: أنه سأل ملك الموت حتى سأل الله - جل وعز - أن رفعه فأدخل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjāj allows that God informed Idrīs about humanity's passage through Hell and their eternal stay in Paradise before revealing the Qur'an, which later agreed with that knowledge.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون قد أعلم الله - عز وجل - إدريس ورود الخلق النار وأنهم مخلدون في الجنان قبل إنزاله القرآن،

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Another report says Idrīs was raised as Jesus was.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أنه رفع كما رفع عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The high place may instead mean Idrīs's elevated rank in prophethood and knowledge.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون - والله أعلم - قوله: (ورفعناه مكانا عليا) أي في النبوة والعلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the prophets hear God's signs, they prostrate and weep from fear of God.
rows.anchor: إذا سمعوا بآيات الله - عز وجل - سجدوا وبكوا من خشية الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بكيا is the plural of باك, like شهود from شاهد and قعود from قاعد.
rows.anchor: و (بكيا) جمع باك، مثل شاهد وشهود وقاعد وقعود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سجدا is a circumstantial accusative describing an intended state: at the instant of falling they are not yet prostrating.
rows.anchor: (سجدا) حال مقدرة المعنى: خروا مقدرين السجود لأن الإنسان في حال خروره لا يكون ساجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating بكيا as a verbal noun is mistaken because it is coordinated with سجدا, a plural noun for those prostrating.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: (بكيا) ههنا مصدر فقد أخطأ لأن (سجدا) جمع ساجد و (بكيا) عطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلف with a still lām normally denotes a bad successor and with fatḥa a good successor, though reversed usage occurs; the first distinction is best.
rows.anchor: يقال في الرداءة خلف - بإسكان اللام - تقول خلف سوء وفي

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: One interpretation says the successors delayed prayer beyond its proper time.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنهم صلوها في غير وقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they abandoned prayer entirely; Zajjāj finds this more fitting because the next verse describes repentance and belief, pointing to disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الأشبه، لأنه يدل على أنه يعنى به الكفار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غيا means the recompense of error, like the recompense called أثاما elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي فسوف يلقون مجازاة الغي كما قال عز وجل: (ومن يفعل ذلك يلق أثاما)

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: The exegesis also identifies غي as a valley or river in Hell; it could be a river prepared for the errant and named Ghayy.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن، (غيا) واد في جهنم، وقيل نهر في جهنم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من can be accusative as an exception from the preceding threat, meaning they will meet punishment except those who repent and believe.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب أي فسوف يلقون العذاب إلا التائبين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, من is an exception from a different class, with the meaning “however, whoever repents and believes.”
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون نصبا استثناء من غير الأول، ويكون المعنى لكن من تاب وآمن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading is noted for يدخلون الجنة.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ - يدخلون الجنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رفع جنات means “they are Gardens of Eden,” while its accusative means “they enter Gardens of Eden”; عدن means residence, from staying in a place.
rows.anchor: يجوز الرفع والنصب، الرفع على معنى هي جنات عدن، والنصب على معنى يدخلون في جنات عدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مأتيا is a passive participle from coming: when something reaches you, you have also reached it; the same reciprocal usage applies to arriving at good fortune.
rows.anchor: ماتي: مفعول من الإتيان، لأن كل ما وصل إليك فقد وصلت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لغو is speech to be discarded and speech that incurs sin; سلام is a comprehensive name for good and safety.
rows.anchor: اللغو ما يلغى من الكلام ويؤثم فيه، و (سلاما) اسم جامع للخير متضمن للسلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise hear only speech that keeps them safe.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أن أهل الجنة لا يسمعون إلا ما يسلمهم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Though Paradise has no actual morning or evening, its provision is described in familiar earthly terms, meaning the span between dawn and evening.
rows.anchor: قيل: ليس ثم بكرة ولا عشي، ولكنهم خوطبوا بما يعقلون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they receive provision every hour; if it is understood as the dawn-to-evening span, that provision meets their wishes at each hour until the next period.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في التفسير أيضا أن معناه: ولهم رزقهم فيها كل ساعة

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel delayed bringing revelation, and the Prophet told him that he had been missed; Gabriel answered with this verse.
rows.anchor: يروى أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أبطأ عنه جبريل عليه السلام في الوحي، فقال عليه السلام وقد أتاه جبريل: ما زرتنا حتى اشتقت إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What lies ahead is the afterlife's reward and punishment; what is behind is all past worldly events; what is between is from now until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ما بين أيدينا امر الآخرة والثواث والعقاب، وما خلفنا جميع ما مضى من أمر الدنيا

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes “what is between” as the interval between the two trumpet blasts.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير وما بين ذلك قيل ما بين النفختين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not forgetful: He knows past, present, and future and preserves them all.
rows.anchor: أي قد علم الله جل وعلا ما كان وما يكون وما هو كائن، حافظ لذلك عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also reassure the Prophet that his Lord had not forgotten him despite the revelation's delay.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون والله أعلم: ما نسيك ربك وإن تأخر عنك الوحي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord owns the heavens and earth and knows them and everything in them.
rows.anchor: أي هو مالك لهما وعالم بهما وبما فيهما

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: The exegesis glosses سميّا as “a likeness” and also says only God has been named al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير: هل تعلم له مثلا، وجاء أيضا لم يسم بالرحمن إلا الله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one but God merits the titles Creator, Powerful, and Knower of past and future.
rows.anchor: يستحق أن يقال له خالق وقادر وعالم بما كان وبما يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person questioning resurrection is specifically the disbeliever who does not believe in the unseen; مت and مت are both forms.
rows.anchor: يعنى بهذا الكافر الذي لا يؤمن بالغيب خاصة، ومت ومت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أولا يذكر has both a light and a doubled reading.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ أو لا يذكر بالتخفيف والتثقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Re-creating people is like their initial creation; the answer to the denier is that the One who first made the bones will revive them.
rows.anchor: أعلم الله عز وجل أن إعادة الخلق مثل ابتداء خلقهم، وهذا كما قال: (وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath promises to resurrect and gather the disbelievers with the devils who led them astray.
rows.anchor: أي فوربك لنبعثنهم ولنحشرنهم مع الشياطين الذين أغووهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جثيا describes them on their knees, unable to stand; it is a plural of جاث like قعود from قاعد and بروك from بارك.
rows.anchor: ومعنى جثيا على ركبهم، لا يستطيعون القيام مما هم فيه وجثي جمع جاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جثيا is accusative as a circumstantial expression; jīm normally has ḍamma, but kasra is allowed by vowel assimilation to yāʾ.
rows.anchor: والأصل ضم الجيم وجائز كسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عتيا can have kasra or ḍamma; from each faction the most insolent are seized first, then those next in degree.
rows.anchor: من كل أمة ومن كل فرقة الأعتى فالأعتى منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical reading has أيهم nominative; accusative is also allowed, reported by Sībawayh and read by Hārūn al-Aʿwar.
rows.anchor: فأما رفع (أيهم) فهو القراءة

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus, as transmitted by Sībawayh, says لننزعن governs nothing; أيهم begins a new question: which of them is most insolent?
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه عن يونس إن قوله جل وعز

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl treats أيهم as a relative-like expression, “those of whom it is said: which is most insolent,” illustrated by a verse about staying where one is neither distressed nor deprived.
rows.anchor: وأما الخليل فحكى عنه سيبويه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says أيهم is built on ḍamma because it uniquely follows a clause-opening particle and can mean أيهم هو أفضل with هو omitted; related forms require هو.
rows.anchor: مبنية على الضم لأنها خالفت أخواتها

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: The accusative remains good despite omitting هو because it may be omitted, as in the reading of “on that which is best,” meaning الذي هو أحسن.
rows.anchor: حذفها، وقد قرئت (تماما على

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq prefers al-Khalīl's analysis: the faction is searched for those singled out as most insolent, which suits the exegesis.
rows.anchor: والذي أعتقده أن القول في هذا قول الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صليا may be read with ḍamma or kasra and is accusative as a circumstantial expression; those most insolent are most deserving of burning.
rows.anchor: وصليا منصوب على الحال.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One view says all people enter Hell, the pious escape, and the wrongdoers are left there; it argues from the verse's general wording and from “leave” implying the wrongdoers are already there.
rows.anchor: إن الخلق جميعا يردون النار

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view limits the warning to polytheists, citing a variant reading منهم rather than منكم; then the saved believers are extracted from those admitted to Hell.
rows.anchor: المشركون خاصة، واحتجوا في هذا بأن بعضهم قرأ

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A third view says all people approach it, but it is cool and safe for believers; they then leave for Paradise, recognizing the blessing by seeing the punished.
rows.anchor: إن الخلق يردونها فتكون على المؤمن بردا وسلاما

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda hold that arrival at Hell does not mean entering it; Arabic usage supports their distinction.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود والحسن وقتادة: إن ورودها ليس دخولها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan's group argues that Arabs say وردت ماء without entering it, as in the Qur'anic account of Moses arriving at Midian's water.
rows.anchor: أن العرب تقول: وردت ماء كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decisive proof that the blessed will not enter Hell is the statement that those granted good are kept away from it and do not hear its faint sound.
rows.anchor: أولئك عنها مبعدون (101) لا يسمعون حسيسها

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's verse says the women reached the water, supporting the Arabic use of ورود for reaching a place without entering it.
rows.anchor: فلما وردن الماء زرقا جمامه وضعن عصي الحاضر المتخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نديا means a gathering or meeting place.
rows.anchor:
خير مقاما وأحسن نديا (73)
(وأحسن نديا).
معناه مجلسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three readings are cited—رئيا, ريا, and زيا—and a fourth, ريئا, is linguistically possible but not reported as a reading.
rows.anchor: فيها أربعة أوجه رئيا بهمزة قبل الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رئيا means fine appearance beside furnishings; unhamzated ريا either drops the hamza with the same sense or suggests luxuriance visibly expressed in their appearance.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى فيه هم أحسن أثاثا أي متاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زيا means good attire or appearance; the accusative phrase explains how the destroyed generations surpassed their successors.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ زيا فمعناه أن زيهم حسن يعني هيئتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ريئا is a metathesized form of رئيا; the verse by the poet Kathīr attests the alternate expression راءني for رآني.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ ريئا فهو بمعنى رئيا مقلوب لأن من العرب من يقول قد راءني زيد

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: Kathīr's poem uses راءني as the form whose inversion supports the variant ريئا.
rows.anchor: وكل خليل راءني فهو قائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative فليمدد conveys a report: God makes the consequence of straying that the strayer remains prolonged in error; the imperative intensifies commitment to that outcome.
rows.anchor: هذا لفظ أمر في معنى الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An imperative can make a report more binding, like “whoever visits me, let me honor him,” which commits the speaker to the act.
rows.anchor: من رآني فلأكرمه، فهو ألزم من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العذاب and الساعة are accusative appositives of ما يوعدون: the punishment is the believers' promised victory through killing and capture, while the Hour brings the promised eternity in Hell.
rows.anchor: العذاب والساعة منصوبان على البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will learn they are weaker than the Prophet's Muslims through defeat, and worse placed through their standing in Hell compared with believers in Paradise.
rows.anchor: أنهم أضعف جندا من جند النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والمسلمين

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A transmitted abrogation analogy says an able person could once feed a poor person and skip the Ramadan fast; obligatory fasting later abrogated that allowance.
rows.anchor: من صوم رمضان من أنه كان يجوز لمن يقدر على الصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may increase the guided in certainty and guidance as He lets a sinner become further astray through sin.
rows.anchor: يجعل جزاءهم أن يزيدهم في يقينهم هدى كما أضل الله الفاسق بفسقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enduring good deeds are righteous acts, foremost among them God's oneness, expressed in the testimony that no deity exists but God.
rows.anchor: الأعمال الصالحة، وأولها توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant الولد with ḍamma can be a plural like أسد, can be singular or plural, or can mean the same as ولد, as with العرب and العجم.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأ ولدا بالضم فهو على وجهين

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: The denier is identified in the exegesis as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء في التفسير أنه يعنى به العاص بن وائل

rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: Khabbāb recounts that as a pre-Islamic blacksmith he was owed money by al-ʿĀṣ, who refused payment unless he rejected Muhammad; Khabbāb refused, and al-ʿĀṣ mockingly promised to repay after resurrection with wealth and children.
rows.anchor: قال: كنت قينا في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the boastful man has seen the unseen or received a covenant from the Merciful; it echoes the claim that he would receive something better if returned to God.
rows.anchor: أي علم ذلك غيبا أم أعطي عهدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا is a rebuke and warning that makes the speaker recognize the error in his claim.
rows.anchor: ردع وتنبيه، أي هذا مما يرتدع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سنكتب ما يقول means God will preserve his words against him.
rows.anchor: (سنكتب ما يقول). أي سنحفظ عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will take away the man's wealth and children, assign them to another, and bring him alone.
rows.anchor: أي نجعل المال والولد لغيره ونسلبه ذلك ويأتينا فردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عزا means helpers or supporters.
rows.anchor: أي أعوانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false gods will become supporters against their worshippers.
rows.anchor: أي يصيرون عليهم أعوانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis says God left the devils and disbelievers together and did not protect the latter from accepting the devils' influence.
rows.anchor: أنا خلينا الشياطين وإياهم، فلم نعصمهم من القبول منهم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq prefers that the devils were assigned to the disbelievers because of their unbelief, as in the verse about a devil being appointed as a companion.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: والوجه الثاني - وهو المختار -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تؤزهم means agitating them until they commit sins; “sending” means giving them power, as in God's statement that Satan has no authority except over his followers.
rows.anchor: معنى (تؤزهم أزا) تزعجهم حتى يركبوا المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وفدا means honored riders who arrive as a delegation.
rows.anchor: معنى الوفد الركبان المكرمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وردا means that the criminals are driven on foot and thirsty.
rows.anchor: مشاة عطاشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من may be nominative, replacing the plural pronoun: only those who took a covenant can own intercession; covenant here means God's testimony and belief in Him.
rows.anchor: فأما الرفع فعلى البدل من الواو والنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively من is accusative as an exception from a different class: wrongdoers lack intercession, but whoever took the covenant has it.
rows.anchor: والنصب على الاستثناء ليس من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إدا is read with fatḥa and means a grave act of disbelief; آدا is another dialectal form, though Zajjāj does not know it to have been read.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ (أدا) - بالفتح - ومعناه شيئا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will create affection for believers in the hearts of other believers.
rows.anchor: أي محبة في قلوب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لدا is the plural of ألد, like صم from أصم, and means people fiercely given to dispute.
rows.anchor: جمع ألد مثل أصم وصم، والألد الشديد الخصومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تحس means perceive or see; حسسهم without the alif can mean he killed them.
rows.anchor: يقال: هل أحسست صاحبك أي هل رأيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ركز is a faint, low sound.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (أو تسمع لهم ركزا). الركز الصوت الخفي.
